Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 29, verses 1–3:

[It is] Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

{1–3} He, exalted is He, informs us of the perfection of His wisdom, and that His wisdom does not require that everyone who says he is a believer and claims faith for himself be left in a state in which they are safe from trials and tribulations, and in which nothing comes upon them that disturbs their faith and its branches. For if the matter were so, the truthful would not be distinguished from the liar, nor the righteous from the falsifier. Rather, His way and custom with the earlier peoples and with this Ummah is that He tests them with ease and hardship, with hardship and ease, with what they like and what they dislike, with wealth and poverty, with the enemies being given power over them at times, and with striving against the enemies by word and deed, and other such trials. All of these trials return to the trial of doubts that oppose belief and desires that oppose the will. Whoever, when doubts arise, keeps firm in his faith and is not shaken, and repels them with the truth he possesses, and, when desires arise that compel and call to sins and misdeeds, or that divert him from what Allah and His Messenger have commanded, acts in accordance with the requirements of faith and strives against his desire, this shows the truthfulness and soundness of his faith. And whoever, when doubts arise, has them affect his heart with doubt and suspicion, and when desires confront him, they turn him toward sins or divert him from obligations, this shows the unsoundness and untruthfulness of his faith. People in this station are of varying ranks that none can count except Allah, from those who are minimal to those who are abundant. So we ask Allah, exalted is He, to make us firm with the firm word in this worldly life and in the Hereafter, and to make our hearts steadfast upon His religion. For trial and examination for souls are like the furnace that brings out their dross and their goodness.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 29, verse 10–11:

{10 – 11} When He (Exalted is He) mentioned that He must test those who claim faith, so that the truthful may be distinguished from the liar, He explained that among people there is a group who have no patience with trials and no steadfastness against certain upheavals. He said: {And among the people is he who says, "We believe in Allah," but when he is harmed for the sake of Allah} – by beating, the seizure of wealth, or reproach – {he regards the trial of people as the punishment of Allah}; that is, he makes it a hindrance to him from faith and from remaining steadfast in it, just as punishment is a hindrance from that which causes it. {And if victory comes from your Lord, they will surely say, "Indeed, we were with you"} – because that agrees with their desires.

This category of people is among those of whom Allah said: {And among the people is he who worships Allah on an edge. If good befalls him, he is reassured by it; but if a trial befalls him, he turns back on his face. He has lost this world and the Hereafter. That is the manifest loss} {Is not Allah most knowing of what is within the breasts of the worlds?} – for He has informed you of this group whose condition is as He described to you, so that you may thereby recognize the perfection of His knowledge and the breadth of His wisdom. {And Allah will surely make evident those who believed, and He will surely make evident the hypocrites} – that is, for this reason He decreed trials and tests, so that His knowledge of them may become manifest, and He may recompense them according to what has appeared from them, not according to what He knows by His knowledge alone; for they may argue against Allah that they would have remained steadfast had they been tested.

{12} He (may He be exalted) informs us of the fabrications of the disbelievers and their invitation of the believers to their religion. Within this is a warning to the believers against being deceived by them and falling into their deception. He said: {And those who disbelieved said to those who believed, "Follow our way"}: that is, abandon your religion, or part of it, and follow us in our religion; for indeed we will bear for you the matter [of consequences], {and we will carry your sins}. This matter is not in their hands. For this reason He said: {But they will not bear anything of their sins}: neither little nor much. This bearing, even if the one who is burdened consents to it, does not benefit at all, for the right belongs to Allah, and Allah, the Exalted, has not empowered the servant to dispose of His right except by His command and His judgment. And His judgment is that {no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another}.

{13} Since His saying {but they will not bear anything of their sins} might lead one to imagine that the disbelievers who call others to their disbelief, and those like them who call to falsehood, bear only the sin they themselves committed and not the sin committed by others, even if they were the cause of it, He said, guarding against this illusion: {And they will surely bear their own burdens}, that is, the burdens of their own sins which they committed, {and other burdens along with their burdens}: these are the sins that occurred because of them and as a consequence of them. So the sin committed by the follower has a share for both the follower and the one followed: for the follower, because he committed and carried it out; and for the one followed, because he caused it and called to it. Just as when the follower performs a good deed, its reward accrues to him by direct performance, and to the one who called to it, his reward accrues by causation. {And they will surely be questioned on the Day of Resurrection about what they used to fabricate}: of evil, and its embellishment, and their saying {and we will carry your sins}.

It seems that these verses are parenthetical between Abraham's speech to his people and their response to him, and God knows best.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 29, verse 24–25:

{24} That is: The response of Ibrahim's people to Ibrahim, when he called them to his Lord, was not acceptance of his call, nor being guided by his counsel, nor seeing the blessing of Allah upon them in sending him to them. Rather, their response to him was the worst of responses. {They said, "Kill him or burn him"}: the most heinous of killings. They were people of power, who had authority, so they threw him into the fire. {But Allah saved him} from it. {Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe}: who know the truth of what the messengers brought, their righteousness and their sincere counsel, and the falsehood of the words of those who opposed and contradicted them, and that the opponents of the messengers were as if they had agreed among themselves and urged one another to deny.

{25} {And he said}: to them, among what he said in his counsel: {Indeed you have taken, instead of Allah, idols out of mutual affection among yourselves in the life of this world}; that is, the ultimate end of that is affection in this world, which will cease and vanish. {Then on the Day of Resurrection, some of you will disbelieve in others and some of you will curse others}; that is, each of the worshippers and the worshipped will disown the other. When people are gathered, they will be enemies to them, and they will disbelieve in their worship. So how can you attach yourselves to one who knows that he will disown his worshippers and curse them? And the abode of all, the worshippers and the worshipped, is {the Fire}, and there is no one who will help them against the punishment of Allah, nor will anyone ward off His retribution from them.

Nevertheless, Lut, whom Allah had designated as a prophet and sent to his people, as will be mentioned later, believed in his call. {And he said}: Ibrahim, when he saw that the call to his people was of no benefit to them: ﴿Indeed, I am a migrant to my Lord﴾; that is, I am emigrating from the land of evil, and migrating to the blessed land, which is al-Sham (Greater Syria). ﴿Indeed, He is the Exalted in Might﴾; that is, the One who possesses strength, and He is able to guide you, but He is the Wise, and His wisdom did not necessitate that.

When he withdrew from them and separated from them while they remained in their state, Allah did not mention regarding them that He destroyed them with a punishment. Rather, He mentioned his withdrawal from them and his emigration from among them. As for what is mentioned in the Isra'iliyyat (narratives derived from Jewish and Christian sources) that Allah opened for his people the gate of gnats, so they drank their blood, ate their flesh, and annihilated them entirely, then the affirmation of this depends upon a legal proof, and none has been found. If Allah had uprooted them with punishment, He would have mentioned it, just as He mentioned the destruction of the nations who denied. But is it among the secrets of this that the Friend (al-Khalil), peace be upon him, was among the most merciful, most excellent, most forbearing and most dignified of creation, so he did not invoke curses upon his people as others did, and Allah would not have brought about a general punishment because of him? And what indicates this is that he argued with the angels concerning the destruction of the people of Lut, disputed with them, and defended them, though they were not his people. And Allah knows best the reality.

{27} ﴿And We gave him Isaac and Jacob﴾; that is, after he migrated to al-Sham. ﴿And We placed in his descendants prophethood and the Book﴾: for no prophet came after him except from his offspring, and no book was revealed except to his descendants, until they were concluded with his son Muhammad (ﷺ), and upon them all. This is among the greatest virtues and distinctions: that the sources of guidance, mercy, happiness, success and triumph should be in his descendants, and through them the guided were guided, the believers believed, and the righteous became righteous. ﴿And We gave him his reward in this world﴾: a beautiful wife of exceptional beauty, abundant provision, children through whom his eye was comforted, and knowledge of Allah, His love, and turning to Him in repentance. ﴿And indeed, he is in the Hereafter among the righteous﴾: rather, he and Muhammad (ﷺ) are the most excellent of the righteous absolutely and the highest in rank. Thus Allah combined for him the happiness of this world and the Hereafter.

It has preceded that Lut (peace be upon him) believed in Ibrahim and became one of those guided by him. They have mentioned that he was not from the descendants of Ibrahim, but rather he was the son of Ibrahim's brother. The statement of the Most High, ﴿And We placed in his descendants prophethood and the Book﴾, even if general, does not contradict Lut being a prophet and messenger, while he is not from his descendants, because the verse was brought in the context of praising and commending the Friend, and it has informed that Lut was guided at his hands. Whoever is guided at his hands is more complete, in terms of the excellence of the guide, than those guided from among his descendants. And Allah knows best.

{44} That is: He, exalted is He, is the One who alone created the heavens, with their loftiness, elevation, vastness and beauty, and what is in them of the sun, the moon, the stars and the angels; and the earth, and what is in it of mountains, seas, deserts, wastelands, trees and the like. {45} He, exalted is He, commands the recitation of His revelation and His sending down, which is this great Book. The meaning of reciting it is: following it by carrying out what it commands and avoiding what it forbids, being guided by its guidance, affirming its reports, contemplating its meanings, and reciting its words. Thus the recitation of its wording is part and a portion of the meaning. Since this is the meaning of reciting the Book, it is known that establishing the whole religion is included in the recitation of the Book. So His saying {And establish the prayer} is an instance of *ʿatf al-khāṣṣ ʿalā al-ʿāmm* (the mention of a specific item after a general one), because of the excellence, nobility, and beautiful effects of the prayer (*ṣalāh*). These effects are stated in His saying {Indeed, the prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing}. *Al-faḥshāʾ* (immorality) is everything among sins that is greatly condemned and considered shameful, which souls desire. *Al-munkar* (wrongdoing) is every sin that minds and natural dispositions reject.

The reason the prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing is that the servant who maintains it, completes its pillars, conditions, and humility, has his heart illuminated, his inner self purified, his faith increased, his desire for good strengthened, and his desire for evil diminished or eliminated. Therefore, by necessity, its constant performance and its preservation in this manner prohibit immorality and wrongdoing. This is among the greatest aims and fruits of the prayer.

There is in the prayer a purpose greater and more significant than this, which is the remembrance of God contained in it by the heart, tongue, and body. God, exalted is He, created the servants only to worship Him, and the most excellent act of worship they perform is the prayer. In it are the acts of worship of all the limbs, which are not found in any other act. For this reason He said {And the remembrance of God is greatest}. It is possible that, when He commanded the prayer and praised it, He informed that His remembrance outside the prayer is greater than the prayer, as is the saying of the majority of the exegetes (*mufassirūn*). However, the first meaning is more correct, because the prayer is more excellent than remembrance outside it, and because it is, as has already been stated, itself among the greatest remembrance. {And God knows what you do}: of good and evil, and He will reward you for that with the most complete and perfect reward.

{46} Allah forbids disputing with the People of the Book when the disputant lacks insight, or when the dispute is not conducted on a sound and acceptable basis, and He commands that they dispute only in the best manner: with good character, gentleness, soft speech, calling to the truth and making it appealing, and refuting falsehood and making its ugliness apparent, by the nearest route that leads to that. The purpose should not be mere disputation, contention, and love of prominence; rather, the purpose should be to clarify the truth and guide the creation. ﴿Except﴾ those among the People of the Book who are wrongdoers: namely, when it becomes apparent from their intention and condition that they have no desire for the truth, and they dispute only for the sake of quarrelsomeness and contention. For such a person there is no benefit in disputing with him, because the purpose of disputation is lost in his case. ﴿And say: "We believe in what has been sent down to us and what has been sent down to you; our God and your God is One"﴾; that is, let your disputation with the People of the Book be founded upon belief in what has been revealed to you and what has been revealed to them, upon belief in your Messenger and their Messenger, and upon the belief that God is One. Let your debate with them not be conducted in a way that results in disparaging any of the divine Books or any of the Messengers, as the ignorant do when debating opponents, disparaging everything they hold, both truth and falsehood. This is wrongdoing and a departure from what is obligatory and from the etiquette of inquiry, for what is obligatory is that the falsehood in the opponent's position be rejected, and the truth in his position be accepted, and the truth not be rejected on account of his saying it, even if he is a disbeliever.

Furthermore, building the debate with the People of the Book on this approach entails obliging them to acknowledge the Qur'an and the Messenger who brought it. For when one speaks of the foundational religious principles on which the Prophets and the Books agree, which are established between the two debaters, whose realities are confirmed in both of them, and which the earlier Books and the Messengers, together with the Qur'an and Muhammad (ﷺ), have explained, indicated, and reported, then it becomes necessary to affirm all the Books and all the Messengers. This is one of the distinctive features of Islam. As for saying, "We believe in what a particular book indicates, but not in another particular book," this is wrongdoing and caprice, and it amounts to a statement of denial; for whoever denies the Qur'an, which indicates these principles and confirms what lies before it of the Torah, is denying what he claims to believe in. Furthermore, every proof by which the prophethood of any prophet whatsoever is established is, in its like and greater, indicative of the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ); and every doubt raised to disparage the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ) can, in its like or greater, be directed against the prophethood of another. So when its falsity is established with regard to another, its falsity with regard to him (ﷺ) is far more evident and clearer. As for His saying, ﴿and to Him we are Muslims﴾; that is, submissive and surrendering to His command. {49} That is, rather, this Qur'an consists of {clear signs}: not hidden things, {in the hearts of those who have been given knowledge}: and they are the leaders of mankind and their intellects, and among them the people of understanding and the perfected ones. For this reason He said: {And none deny Our signs except the wrongdoers}: because none denies them except an ignorant person who speaks without knowledge and does not follow the people of knowledge, while he is able to know it as it truly is; or a willful one who knows that it is the truth but opposes it out of obstinacy, and knows its truthfulness yet turns against it.

{50} That is: these wrongdoers, who deny the Messenger and what he brought, objected and proposed that certain specific signs be sent down, as when they said: ﴿We will not believe you until you cause a spring to gush for us from the earth…﴾ and the rest of the verses. Specifying the signs is not for them, nor for the Messenger (ﷺ), for in that there is a presumption to plan alongside God, saying "if it were such," or "it should be such." No one has any say in the matter. Therefore He said: ﴿Say: The signs are only with God﴾, meaning that if He wills, He sends them down or withholds them, ﴿and I am only a clear warner﴾, meaning I have no rank above this rank. Since the purpose is to make clear the truth from falsehood, once the aim is achieved by whatever means, proposing specific signs is wrongdoing, injustice and arrogance toward God and toward the truth. Moreover, even if those signs were sent down and they still held in their hearts that they would not believe in the truth except because of them, that would not be faith. It would be merely something that agreed with their desires, so they believed not because it is true but because of those signs. So what benefit would come from sending them down, even on that hypothetical assumption?

{51} Since the aim is to make the truth clear, He, exalted is He, mentioned its method, saying: ﴿Is it not sufficient for them﴾, in their knowledge of your truthfulness and the truthfulness of what you brought, ﴿that We have sent down to you the Book, which is recited to them﴾. This is a concise yet comprehensive statement, containing much of the clear signs and striking proofs. As has already been mentioned, the Messenger's bringing it alone, while he was unlettered, is among the greatest signs of his truthfulness. Then there is their inability to produce its like, and its challenge to them to bring another such thing. Then its manifestation and open proclamation, being recited to them and said to be from God. The Messenger made it known while his supporters were few and his opponents and enemies were many; yet he did not conceal it, and this did not weaken his resolve. Rather, he declared it openly before the assemblies and proclaimed it among settled and nomadic people: that this is the speech of my Lord. So is there anyone who can oppose it, produce its equal, or match it? Then there is its report of the stories of the earlier peoples, the accounts of the past, and the unseen matters of the past and future, all corresponding to reality. Then its supremacy over the earlier Books, its confirmation of what is sound in them, and its denial of the distortion and alteration that entered them. Then its guidance to the right path in its commands and prohibitions: it never commands something of which reason would say, "I wish it had not commanded it," nor forbids something of which reason would say, "I wish it had not forbidden it." Rather, it accords with justice, the balance and the wisdom that is understood by those of insight and intellect. Then its adaptation of its guidance and rulings to every condition and every time, such that affairs are set right only by it. {56–59} He, exalted is He, says: "O My servants who have believed" in Me and affirmed My Messenger, "indeed, My earth is spacious, so worship Me alone." If it becomes impossible for you to worship your Lord in one land, then migrate from it to another land where worship is for Allah alone. The places and sites of worship are spacious, the One worshipped is one, and death will certainly descend upon you, and then you will be returned to your Lord. He will reward whoever perfected his worship and combined faith with righteous deeds by bestowing upon him the lofty chambers and the beautiful, comprehensive dwellings, containing what the souls desire and what the eyes find delight in, "and you therein will abide forever." How excellent are those dwellings in the Gardens of Bliss as a reward for those who act for Allah.

"Those who are patient" in worshipping Allah, "and upon their Lord they rely" in that. Their patience in worshipping Allah requires exerting effort and energy in it, and a great struggle against Satan, who calls them to neglect some of it. Their reliance (tawakkul) requires a strong dependence upon Allah and a good opinion of Him, that He will fulfill and complete the deeds they have resolved upon. Tawakkul is mentioned explicitly, although it is included within patience, because it is needed in every action and in abandoning every thing commanded, and it is not complete without it.

{60} That is: The Creator, blessed and exalted, has undertaken the provision of all creatures, the strong and the weak alike. {61–63} This is an argument against the polytheists who denied tawhid of worship (tawhid al-uluhiyyah), and a binding of them to what they themselves affirmed, namely tawhid of lordship (tawhid al-rububiyyah). For if you were to ask them, "Who created the heavens and the earth?" and "Who sends down water from the sky, giving life thereby to the earth after its death?" and "Who controls the management of all things?" they would surely say, "God" alone. They would have acknowledged the incapacity of the idols and of those they worshipped besides God in any of these matters! But when the hardship is removed from them and He delivers them, by means of those to whom they sincerely directed their supplication, to dry land, they associate with Him those who neither delivered them from any hardship nor removed from them any difficulty. Why, then, did they not make their supplication sincerely to God in times of ease and hardship, and in times of comfort and adversity, so that they might be truly believers in Him, deserving His reward and having His punishment averted from them? Yet this polytheism of theirs came after Our blessing upon them of deliverance from the sea, so that its outcome would be ingratitude for what We have given them and repaying blessing with evil, and so that they might complete their enjoyment in the world, which is like the enjoyment of cattle, having no concern but their bellies and their private parts. ﴿So they will come to know.﴾ When they move from the world to the Hereafter, the intensity of regret and the painfulness of punishment.

{67} Then He bestowed favor upon them by making His sanctuary secure, and by making them its people, in safety, ease and provision, while people around them are snatched away and live in fear. ﴿Will they not worship the Lord of this House, who fed them against hunger and made them safe from fear?﴾ ﴿Will they then believe in falsehood?﴾ That is, what they are upon of polytheism, and false sayings and false deeds, ﴿and be ungrateful for the favor of God?﴾ Where has their intellect gone, and their judgment been stripped away, since they preferred error to guidance, falsehood to truth, and misery to happiness, and since they became the most wrongdoing of creatures?

{68} ﴿And who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against God,﴾ attributing to God what they are upon of error and falsehood, ﴿or denies the truth when it has come to him?﴾ Through His messenger Muhammad (ﷺ). But this unjust and obstinate one has Hell before him. ﴿Is there not in Hell an abode for the disbelievers?﴾ Where their right will be taken from them, they will be disgraced by it, and it will be their permanent dwelling from which they will never leave?

{69} ﴿And those who strive in Us﴾: they are those who emigrated in the way of God, struggled against their enemies, and exerted their effort in seeking His pleasure. ﴿We will surely guide them to Our paths﴾; that is, the ways that lead to Us. This is because they are doers of good. ﴿And indeed, God is with the doers of good﴾ by aid, victory and guidance.

This indicates that the people most deserving of conformity to what is right are the people of jihad. It also indicates that whoever does well in what he has been commanded will be aided by God, and He will facilitate for him the means of guidance. It further indicates that whoever exerts himself and strives in seeking sacred knowledge, there will come to him, from guidance and help in attaining his aim, matters of divine origin that lie beyond the grasp of his effort, and the matter of knowledge will be made easy for him. Indeed, seeking sacred knowledge is among jihad in the way of God; rather, it is one of the two kinds of jihad, which only the elite of creation undertake: jihad by speech and tongue against the disbelievers and hypocrites, and striving in teaching the matters of religion and in refuting those who oppose the truth, even if they are among the Muslims.

The commentary on Surah al-'Ankabut is complete, by the praise and help of God.
